oauthOidc.title: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
oauthOidc.subtitle: Authorization Code + PKCE · fixture preview
oauthOidc.outcome: Understand the roles, browser redirects and server-side boundaries behind a secure sign-in journey.
oauthOidc.objective: Explain how a browser, confidential client and provider work together, and why API authorization is a separate decision.

user.label: Human user
user.description: The person initiating the journey. The human, rather than the SPA, is the Resource Owner.

browser.label: Browser / SPA
browser.description: Displays the playground and follows browser redirects. It is not the OAuth client in this architecture.

bff.label: NestJS BFF
bff.description: The proposed confidential client owns transactions, server-held tokens and the application session. No backend is connected to this preview.

authorization-server.label: Authorization Server
authorization-server.description: Handles authorization requests and code exchange. This logical role shares the Keycloak deployment with the Identity Provider.

identity-provider.label: Identity Provider
identity-provider.description: Authenticates the user in Keycloak’s UI. This is a logical role, not a second deployed server or an original OAuth 2.0 role.

resource-server.label: Resource Server
resource-server.description: Independently validates the Access Token and permissions before returning synthetic data in a future runnable mission.

roles.title: Understand the actors
roles.explanation: Separate the human user, browser, OAuth client, Authorization Server, Identity Provider and Resource Server. Two Keycloak roles share one deployment.

authorization.title: Follow the front channel
authorization.explanation: In a real flow, the BFF initiates a redirect and the browser navigates to Keycloak. This preview never starts authentication or leaves for a provider.

identity.title: Locate authentication
identity.explanation: Credentials belong in Keycloak’s login experience. The playground does not provide a password form or observe provider-internal authentication.

exchange.title: Examine the back channel
exchange.explanation: The BFF correlates the callback, exchanges the code directly with Keycloak and validates the OIDC response. A successful exchange would not directly instrument Keycloak’s internal checks.

tokens.title: Distinguish token purposes
tokens.explanation: An ID Token conveys the authentication result to the client. An Access Token is used at the Resource Server. Neither belongs in this inspector.

resource.title: Find the API boundary
resource.explanation: A session alone does not prove API authorization. The Resource Server must check the intended audience, issuer, lifetime, trust and permission.

evidence.title: Review evidence limits
evidence.explanation: Load the fixture samples to explore safe explanatory fields. None is an observed trace; no authentication, API permission or session outcome is demonstrated.

preview.note: Fixture-only preview. Samples explain a possible journey; no network operation, authentication or session is created.

authorization-example.title: Browser authorization redirect
authorization-example.summary: An example of the browser following a BFF-initiated redirect to the Authorization Server. No redirect occurred.
authorization-example.explanation: The BFF is the OAuth client. It creates the authorization transaction; the browser carries the request to Keycloak. A learning checkpoint cannot pause or execute this redirect.

provider-internal-example.title: Provider-internal PKCE binding
provider-internal-example.summary: A teaching note about a provider-internal check, not an instrumented event.
provider-internal-example.explanation: The Authorization Server checks the verifier against the original challenge during code exchange. A BFF could observe the exchange outcome, but cannot claim a direct trace of this internal check.

exchange-example.title: Direct code exchange
exchange-example.summary: An example of direct BFF-to-provider communication. No exchange or session was created.
exchange-example.explanation: The BFF exchanges the authorization code and validates the OIDC response before establishing a session. Tokens stay server-side. This fixture contains no code, verifier, token response, or session result.

resource-example.title: Independent resource authorization
resource-example.summary: An example of a protected-resource boundary. No resource request was sent or permitted.
resource-example.explanation: A Resource Server independently validates trust, issuer, audience, lifetime and permission for an Access Token. An ID Token describes an authentication result for the client and is not an API access credential.

epa.title: ePA / gematik
epa.subtitle: Protected-system boundaries · conceptual layout
epa.outcome: Explore a conceptual map of identity, authorization and protected-system responsibilities in an ePA journey.
epa.objective: Test how different actors and security boundaries fit the workspace. Exact protocol choreography is a future specification decision.

insured-person.label: Insured person
insured-person.description: Illustrative initiator of a protected ePA journey. No real patient or medical data is used.

fdv.label: FdV / client
fdv.description: Illustrative user-facing access channel. This layout does not imply an implemented browser-based FdV.

sectoral-idp.label: Sectoral IdP
sectoral-idp.description: Illustrative authentication or federation responsibility, when applicable to a future specified scenario.

epa-authorization.label: ePA Authorization Service
epa-authorization.description: A conceptual authorization boundary. No ePA authorization operation is implemented or demonstrated.

vau.label: ePA system / VAU
vau.description: A protected subsystem and secure-communication topic to model separately. No live TI connection, exact sequence, or certification is claimed.

actors.title: Discover responsibilities
actors.explanation: These actor types test the layout. They do not imply that every actor participates in one sequence or that a specific ePA scenario has been implemented.

identity.title: Examine identity boundaries
identity.explanation: Identify where identity or federation responsibilities could belong. Current applicable gematik specifications must determine the future scenario.

authorization.title: Inspect authorization boundaries
authorization.explanation: Identity and authorization responsibilities are distinct. This conceptual map specifies no requests, decisions, credentials or operational results.

protected.title: Understand protected systems
protected.explanation: A protected subsystem and secure-communication boundary need their own specification. No VAU behavior is simulated here.

evidence.title: Separate concept from evidence
evidence.explanation: There is no live integration, telemetry or simulated operational result. The empty timeline is intentional. This preview makes no gematik compliance or certification claim.

preview.note: Planned — no live integration, telemetry or simulated operational results. Actor placement is conceptual and does not define a protocol sequence.

catalog.heading: Understand the flow.
catalog.intro: Explore authentication and authorization through actors, explanations and safe evidence. Choose a preview to enter Mission Control.
catalog.noticeTitle: A place to explore, with honest evidence.
catalog.notice: These previews use fixture content. No sign-in, protected API call or live protocol integration runs here. Planned missions stay planned until their real execution is verified.

principles.label: How Mission Control works
principles.actors: Understand who is responsible for each part of a journey.
principles.explanation: Explore checkpoints at your pace, independent of execution.
principles.evidence: Separate what can be observed from what is being explained.

workspace.checkpointNote: Checkpoint selection is learning navigation. It does not execute a flow.
workspace.context: Select an actor, checkpoint or fixture sample to explore its context.

announcements.loaded: Fixture samples loaded. No live operation occurred.
announcements.replayed: Explanation replayed from the first fixture sample.
announcements.reset: View reset. Loaded fixture samples are preserved.
announcements.fitted: Map at readable size. Scroll horizontally to reach additional participants.
